pathway.title: Element Solutions Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Revenue is durable but tied to one cycle. Customers reorder products consumed in their production lines and no customer reaches 10% of net sales, but Electronics is 77.5% of nine-month 2026 net sales and 76.2% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, order backlog is minimal and organic growth of 13% leans on AI infrastructure demand, so a demand slowdown would reach earnings within quarters. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8

Margin resilience is better than reported margins suggest. Gross margin fell to 35.51% in nine months 2026 from 42.34%, and Adjusted EBITDA over total net sales fell by 2.86 percentage points to 19.08%, but pass-through metals of 31.7% of net sales add sales at little margin, and the issuer's margin excluding them rose by 110 bp to 27.9%. Creditors should therefore track EBITDA dollars and the ex-metals margin, not margin on total sales. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62

Cash conversion weakened in 2026 and is the main watch point. Working capital absorbed USD 174.1 million in nine months 2026 against USD 78.4 million a year earlier as metal prices rose, so operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 108.8 million against USD 153.5 million, and dividends and buybacks of USD 97.0 million took most of it. The last-twelve-months figure of USD 182.9 million shows the drag is partly timing. Basis: calculation C04; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

Leverage is the weakest dimension. Net debt of USD 1,857.2 million is 3.29x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, or 2.76x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, because debt was drawn in full for acquisitions whose earnings enter from closing; the reported ratio therefore overstates run-rate leverage, while the adjusted ratio depends on add-backs that include USD 52.6 million of integration and transaction costs in nine months 2026. A USD 100.0 million shortfall in last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage on that measure from 2.76x to 3.24x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C07

Liquidity is adequate and the maturity wall is distant but not covered. Cash of USD 224.9 million and USD 478.0 million of undrawn revolver total USD 702.9 million against USD 800.0 million of notes due 2028-09-01, a USD 97.1 million shortfall that cash generation or a refinancing must close. The springing first lien test applies only if revolver borrowings exceed USD 150.0 million, USD 135.0 million above today's draw, and the reported covenant ratio is not printed. Basis: calculation C05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Interest rate risk returns before the 2030 maturities. About 94% of debt is fixed through swaps, which hold the effective term loan rate near 4.4%, but swaps covering USD 690 million expire in December 2028 and USD 483 million in December 2029, and refinancing the 2028 notes at a higher coupon adds USD 8.0 million of annual interest for each 100 bp, 9.3% of last-twelve-months cash interest. Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 9

Financial policy risk is medium. No controlling sponsor is identified and the dividend is modest, but acquisitions and buybacks proceeded while leverage rose, and the merger with Solstice was agreed and terminated within weeks, which shows appetite for transformative deals. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12

runs.text: The principal strengths are recurring consumable demand across a diversified customer base, interest cover of 6.59x supported by fixed-rate funding, liquidity of USD 702.9 million with no bullet maturity before 2028, and a record of prepaying debt from disposal proceeds. The principal weaknesses are leverage after debt-funded acquisitions, concentration in Electronics with minimal backlog, working capital absorbing cash in 2026, and USD 800.0 million of notes due in 2028 against present liquidity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Two acquisitions and one refinancing shaped 2026. EFC Gases & Advanced Materials closed on 2026-01-02 for about USD 367 million in cash, funded from cash on hand, with an earn-out of up to USD 30.0 million. Micromax closed on 2026-02-02 for about USD 494 million, funded with USD 450 million of add-on term loans, which have the same terms and the 2030-12-18 maturity as the existing term loans, and revolver borrowings. On the same day the company replaced its USD 375 million revolver with a five-year USD 500 million secured revolving facility maturing in 2031, priced at Term SOFR plus 1.50% a year, and swapped USD 350 million of the add-on term loans into fixed-rate euro debt through December 2029. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126

The proposed Solstice merger of 2026-07-06 would have exchanged each share for half a Solstice share and USD 10.00 in cash and was terminated on 2026-08-27 by mutual agreement with a release of claims. No new notes were issued in the periods supplied, and the only dated debt maturity before 2030 is the USD 800 million senior notes due 2028-09-01. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_esi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.value: Creditors should read 2026 as an acquisition year: two acquisitions closed in January and February 2026, and the proposed merger with Solstice was announced in July and terminated on 2026-08-27, so the third-quarter filings control wherever earlier ones differ. Governance and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the two acquisition prices differ between filings. The filings summarise the facilities, the security package and one springing first lien net leverage test, so Legal & covenants cannot be assessed and any covenant, priority or recovery conclusion would rest on summaries only. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Element Solutions is a widely held, acquisitive specialty-chemicals group with no controlling sponsor identified, so governance risk is medium and rests on financial policy rather than extraction: debt-funded 2026 acquisitions and buybacks are the behaviours creditors should monitor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business sells consumable electronics and industrial materials with no customer at 10% of net sales, but Electronics is 77.5% of nine-month 2026 net sales and the two acquisitions closed in January and February 2026 added USD 389.3 million to nine-month net sales. A merger with Solstice was agreed on 2026-07-06 and terminated on 2026-08-27 with a mutual release and no payment stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is a consumables franchise whose revenue visibility is short. Customers reorder products consumed in their production lines and none reaches 10% of net sales, which limits single-customer loss, but order backlog is minimal, so a fall in electronics demand reaches revenue within quarters rather than being cushioned by contracted volume. Electronics produced 76.2% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026, so creditors are exposed to one demand cycle, led by the AI infrastructure demand that management itself cites.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions have changed the credit profile within one year. Micromax and EFC cost USD 861 million in cash, were funded by USD 450 million of add-on term loans plus cash and revolver borrowings, and brought USD 389.3 million of nine-month 2026 net sales, 13.8% of the total. The purchase accounting assigns USD 235.0 million and USD 172.0 million to identifiable intangibles and USD 128.9 million and USD 163.8 million to goodwill, USD 699.7 million of the USD 877.0 million total consideration, so most of the price is intangible value that depends on the acquired earnings arriving, and EFC executives hold performance units that vest on 2028 and 2030 EFC earnings, so the full cost stays open until then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk is medium on the evidence available. No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, the company is listed, and the documented behaviours are mostly ordinary: a fixed quarterly dividend, USD 200 million of term loan prepayment funded by the 2025 sale of the printing plate business, and a related-party advisory fee of USD 2.0 million a year, which is 0.37% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA and was extended on 2026-05-05 to a three-year term. The softer signal is capital return while leverage was rising: dividends and buybacks of USD 97.0 million in nine months 2026 absorbed 50.5% of operating cash flow, with all of the USD 37.7 million of buybacks in the third quarter, almost all of it in September after the merger was terminated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The terminated Solstice merger shows willingness to pursue a transformative transaction. The agreement of 2026-07-06 would have made the company a wholly owned subsidiary of Solstice for half a Solstice share and USD 10.00 in cash per share, and carried a possible company termination fee of USD 376 million, which would have been paid from cash or the revolver. The termination on 2026-08-27 removed that contingency and the change of control, and no payment is stated, but the company has shown that a large combination is on its agenda, and the change-of-control terms of its notes and loans are not available to test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but has three definitional soft spots. The adjusted EBITDA margin moved in 2026 to a denominator that excludes pass-through metals, prior-year amounts were reclassified without quantification, and annual-report purchase prices for both acquisitions differ from the later quarterly figures. None blocks monitoring, and each is logged in the conflict register, but together they mean year-on-year margin comparisons must be rebuilt rather than read across.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk reading is that the business is better protected than backlog and concentration suggest: products are consumed in manufacturing, the customer base is diversified, switching costs are described as high, and management reports third-quarter organic growth of 13% with record results. That supports a lower governance and business risk reading if growth proves durable and the acquisitions integrate as presented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to high risk if capital returns were debt-funded while leverage stayed elevated, for instance buybacks continuing at the third-quarter pace of USD 37.7 million a quarter while revolver borrowings rise, or if a further large combination were announced before the 2026 acquisitions are absorbed. It would move to low risk if the proxy statement showed independent board control and no related-party leakage beyond the advisory fee, and if the credit agreement showed restricted-payment capacity that is tight relative to current leverage. Evidence that electronics demand is slowing, such as falling organic growth in the Electronics segment from 18% in nine months 2026, would raise business risk independently of governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by debt-funded acquisitions and continued capital returns, because they raise leverage while leaving little retained cash, which implies higher refinancing risk in 2028; countervailing evidence is the 2025 voluntary prepayment, the modest fixed dividend and the absence of any identified controlling sponsor or documented extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two acquisitions and one refinancing shaped 2026. EFC Gases & Advanced Materials closed on 2026-01-02 for about USD 367 million in cash, funded from cash on hand, with an earn-out of up to USD 30.0 million. Micromax closed on 2026-02-02 for about USD 494 million, funded with USD 450 million of add-on term loans, which have the same terms and the 2030-12-18 maturity as the existing term loans, and revolver borrowings. On the same day the company replaced its USD 375 million revolver with a five-year USD 500 million secured revolving facility maturing in 2031, priced at Term SOFR plus 1.50% a year, and swapped USD 350 million of the add-on term loans into fixed-rate euro debt through December 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The proposed Solstice merger of 2026-07-06 would have exchanged each share for half a Solstice share and USD 10.00 in cash and was terminated on 2026-08-27 by mutual agreement with a release of claims. No new notes were issued in the periods supplied, and the only dated debt maturity before 2030 is the USD 800 million senior notes due 2028-09-01.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Element Solutions has an adequate fundamental credit profile: consumable-driven, diversified earnings and 6.59x interest cover support debt service, but debt-funded 2026 acquisitions lifted net leverage to 3.29x, so creditors rely on acquired earnings arriving before the USD 800.0 million notes mature in 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage was 2.13x at the 2025 year-end and is 3.96x pro forma for the two acquisitions closed on 2026-01-02 and 2026-02-02, before any acquired earnings; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA it is 2.76x at 2026-09-30. Cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 702.9 million covers 0.88x of the 2028 notes, and covenant headroom cannot be measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is durable but tied to one cycle. Customers reorder products consumed in their production lines and no customer reaches 10% of net sales, but Electronics is 77.5% of nine-month 2026 net sales and 76.2% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, order backlog is minimal and organic growth of 13% leans on AI infrastructure demand, so a demand slowdown would reach earnings within quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is better than reported margins suggest. Gross margin fell to 35.51% in nine months 2026 from 42.34%, and Adjusted EBITDA over total net sales fell by 2.86 percentage points to 19.08%, but pass-through metals of 31.7% of net sales add sales at little margin, and the issuer's margin excluding them rose by 110 bp to 27.9%. Creditors should therefore track EBITDA dollars and the ex-metals margin, not margin on total sales.

fields.value: Cash conversion weakened in 2026 and is the main watch point. Working capital absorbed USD 174.1 million in nine months 2026 against USD 78.4 million a year earlier as metal prices rose, so operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 108.8 million against USD 153.5 million, and dividends and buybacks of USD 97.0 million took most of it. The last-twelve-months figure of USD 182.9 million shows the drag is partly timing.

fields.value: Leverage is the weakest dimension. Net debt of USD 1,857.2 million is 3.29x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, or 2.76x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, because debt was drawn in full for acquisitions whose earnings enter from closing; the reported ratio therefore overstates run-rate leverage, while the adjusted ratio depends on add-backs that include USD 52.6 million of integration and transaction costs in nine months 2026. A USD 100.0 million shortfall in last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage on that measure from 2.76x to 3.24x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and the maturity wall is distant but not covered. Cash of USD 224.9 million and USD 478.0 million of undrawn revolver total USD 702.9 million against USD 800.0 million of notes due 2028-09-01, a USD 97.1 million shortfall that cash generation or a refinancing must close. The springing first lien test applies only if revolver borrowings exceed USD 150.0 million, USD 135.0 million above today's draw, and the reported covenant ratio is not printed.

fields.value: Interest rate risk returns before the 2030 maturities. About 94% of debt is fixed through swaps, which hold the effective term loan rate near 4.4%, but swaps covering USD 690 million expire in December 2028 and USD 483 million in December 2029, and refinancing the 2028 notes at a higher coupon adds USD 8.0 million of annual interest for each 100 bp, 9.3% of last-twelve-months cash interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy risk is medium. No controlling sponsor is identified and the dividend is modest, but acquisitions and buybacks proceeded while leverage rose, and the merger with Solstice was agreed and terminated within weeks, which shows appetite for transformative deals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest argument for a stronger profile is that leverage is lower than it looks. Issuer-adjusted net leverage is 2.76x, interest cover is 6.59x, 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to about USD 720 million including full-year contributions from both acquisitions, and last-twelve-months operating cash flow less capital expenditure of USD 182.9 million compares with USD 227.6 million in FY2025, so the 2026 drag is partly timing. If fourth-quarter results confirm the guidance and working capital reverses as metal prices stabilise, net leverage on a full-year earnings base would fall without any debt repayment.

fields.value: Element Solutions formulates specialty chemistries and materials that customers consume in manufacturing, in two segments: Electronics, which supplies assembly materials, circuit-board and semiconductor chemistries and, since 2026-02-02, advanced inks and pastes, and Specialties, which supplies industrial surface finishing and offshore energy fluids and, since 2026-01-02, high-purity specialty gases. Because products are consumed in production and replaced as customers produce, revenue recurs without contracted backlog, and the electronics share of net sales has risen to 77.5% with the acquisitions; this supports cash-flow visibility in normal demand but ties debt service to electronics hardware output and to the integration of two acquired businesses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is a listed Delaware corporation with no controlling sponsor identified, so extraction by an owner is not a documented risk; the group borrows through the parent and its co-borrower MacDermid, Incorporated, guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries on a first-lien secured basis, while the 2028 notes carry senior unsecured guarantees from generally the same subsidiaries. The related-party advisory fee of USD 2.0 million a year is small, and the sponsor and governance risk level from Business & governance is medium because capital returns and acquisitions continued as leverage rose and the proxy statement and executed loan documents were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Volume growth is led by AI infrastructure and other high-performance electronics, with Electronics organic growth of 18% against 2% for Specialties in nine months 2026, while reported growth of 50% is lifted by acquisitions and by pass-through metals pricing of USD 891.6 million of net sales. Pricing power is shown by the issuer's margin excluding metals rising rather than falling, switching costs from customer qualification, and no customer at 10% of net sales; the exposure is that metal price moves change reported sales and working capital without changing underlying demand, and that minimal backlog gives no contractual cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Selling, technical, general and administrative expense fell to 21.24% of net sales in nine months 2026 from 25.13%, partly because metals inflate the denominator, and capital expenditure of USD 62.2 million in FY2025 shows a modest fixed-asset base because the company blends purchased raw materials rather than manufacturing basic chemicals. Acquisition, integration and transaction costs of USD 52.6 million were added back to Adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026, so margin defence depends on integration costs ending; specialties margin fell in the third quarter on higher corporate cost allocation, which is the segment to watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure was 2.44% of FY2025 net sales and is expected at about USD 110 million for 2026 for Kuprion capacity and plant consolidation, so free cash flow of USD 227.6 million in FY2025 was 41.56% of Adjusted EBITDA and covered the dividend of USD 77.8 million 2.93 times. In 2026 working capital, higher cash interest and integration costs reduced conversion, and capital expenditure can be deferred as the main flexible lever, with dividends and buybacks the next.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate: named competitors include larger groups, but competition is on qualification, technology and service, which favours incumbents with embedded products. New entrants face qualification and technical-service barriers, which protects margin; substitutes arise through technology change such as chromium-free plating, which the company addresses with research and development. Buyer power is limited by diversification, as no customer reaches 10% of net sales, but large electronics manufacturers can resist price outside qualified products; supplier power is low for most raw materials, which are obtainable from multiple sources, with metals priced through to customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and trade factors are material: tariffs and trade policy can change cost and demand, and about 79% of FY2025 net sales came from outside the United States, so currency translation and geopolitical disruption affect reported results; the economic driver that matters most is metal prices, which move sales and working capital. Interest-rate exposure is largely hedged until the swaps expire in December 2028 and December 2029, and the technological driver is AI-related electronics demand, which sets the growth rate of the largest segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are consumable recurring demand, no customer at 10% of net sales, interest cover of 6.59x and USD 702.9 million of liquidity; weaknesses are electronics concentration, higher leverage after the acquisitions, working-capital absorption and covenant opacity. Opportunities that would improve credit quality are acquired earnings arriving ahead of guidance and early refinancing of the 2028 notes; threats are an electronics demand slowdown, a metal price reversal that strains working capital, and a further large transaction before integration is complete.

Free cash flow would fall toward the distributions it funds, and a USD 100.0 million fall in last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage on that measure to 3.24x, while headroom to the springing first lien test of 5.0 to 1.0 cannot be measured because its definition is not printed. Management levers are deferring capital expenditure of about USD 110 million, suspending buybacks and using the revolver, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2028, but the notes then fall due against liquidity of USD 702.9 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Element Solutions presents an adequate business profile supported by consumable recurring demand, customer diversification and strong interest cover, but credit quality is constrained by higher leverage after debt-funded acquisitions and concentration in Electronics. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to modest capital intensity and a fixed-rate cost of debt, with 2026 working-capital drag expected to be partly timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of acquired earnings, early action on the 2028 notes and the rate environment when swaps expire. The primary downside path is an electronics demand slowdown while leverage is elevated and capital returns continue. Further analysis would require covenant definitions, ratings and market pricing, and acquired earnings. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: leverage after debt-funded acquisitions.
